transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I’m just so tired. It's gotten to the point where I can barely get through a shift at work. It's hard to explain, but it feels heavy, um, like my body is just filled with wet sand or something. And the worst part is that resting doesn’t really bring me back. I just can't shake it.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did the fatigue first start?

Um, honestly, I'm not really sure. It's hard to pinpoint exactly when it started. It kind of just crept up on me, I guess, so I don't have an exact day or week to give you. It just feels like it's been a while now that I've been dragging like this.
Besides feeling tired, have you noticed a change in your mood, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Um, my mood has just been really down. And as for things I usually enjoy... I don't know, it all just feels flat now. Like, I usually love cooking for myself, playing my guitar, going hiking, or even just heading over to my family's place. But lately, when I do those things, it's like I'm just going through the motions. I feel like I'm only pretending to care about them.
How long have you been feeling this way—down and uninterested in things you used to enjoy—has it been more than two weeks now?

Yeah, it's definitely been more than two weeks. I'd say this low, empty feeling has been going on for about four months now. It started a while after this period where I had this huge rush of energy at work, but once that passed, this just sort of settled in.

You mentioned having a period of a big rush of energy at work before this low feeling started—can you tell me more about that time? For example, did you need less sleep than usual, feel unusually confident or talkative, or notice your thoughts racing?

Yeah, during that time I just had so much energy. I was taking on a lot more at work. I volunteered to do extra work in the cash-office, and I started reorganizing all the shelves. I even planned out this whole promotion binder. And the weird thing is, after doing all that all day, I'd go home and still feel wired. I'd be up wanting to buy things online and completely rearrange my apartment. I just couldn't stop doing things.
How long did that period of high energy and increased activity last—was it just a day or two, or did it go on for several days or more?
It was definitely more than just a day or two. Um, that whole thing went on for about a month, actually. It started right around the time the store changed our hours during the remodel.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight gain or weight loss over these past few months?

Yeah, I think I've lost some weight. My appetite has been kind of all over the place, honestly. But lately, I mostly just forget to eat, or when I do try, food just tastes like cardboard. I haven't stepped on a scale or anything, but my work pants have definitely been fitting a lot looser.
During that month when you had all that extra energy, did you also notice things like feeling unusually hot, sweating more than normal, a racing heart, or trembling hands?

Um, no, not really. I didn't notice feeling unusually hot or sweating more than normal. And my hands weren't shaking or anything like that. I just felt really awake and driven, but physically... like with my heart and everything, I felt pretty normal.
During this current period of feeling down and fatigued, have you noticed feeling unusually cold, having dry skin, or being more constipated than usual?
No, I haven't really noticed any of that. I don't feel colder than usual, and my skin seems fine. I haven't had any issues with constipation either. Just mostly the tiredness and not wanting to eat.

During that month of high energy, did it cause any serious problems—like conflicts at work, trouble with relationships, or any dangerous decisions—or was anyone concerned enough that you needed hospitalization?

Yeah, it definitely caused some problems. Um, at work, I started making a lot of mistakes at the register, and I fell really far behind on my cash-office tasks. My manager actually had to take me off some of the responsibilities I was doing... which sucks, because I was hoping those would help me get promoted. 

And, well, with people... I've been avoiding my family a lot. It just got to be too much. I actually had to get some same-day crisis help recently, too, because I just... I didn't feel safe trying to handle everything on my own anymore. So, yeah, it hasn't been great.

During that month when you were extremely energetic and driven, did you ever have any unusual experiences—like hearing or seeing things others didn't, or having beliefs that seemed very intense or hard to shake, such as feeling especially powerful or suspicious of others?

Um, yeah, actually... I did. When I was working at the register, I started hearing voices. It sounded exactly like customers were standing right behind me, just whispering my name. Or they would say things about how I was messing everything up. But every time I turned around to look, nobody was there. It was really strange.

Now, during this current period of feeling down and exhausted, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having beliefs that others might find unusual or hard to shake?

No, not right now. The whispering voices... they really only happened during that wired stretch, you know? When I was barely sleeping, trying to do a million things at work, and my brain just felt like it was racing all the time. I had never heard them before that. And once I crashed and started feeling so exhausted and down, the voices just stopped. So, no, I haven't heard or seen anything unusual lately.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about unusual experiences like hearing or seeing things others didn't (hallucinations) or intense, unshakeable beliefs (delusions) during the energetic period. S020 (Hallucinations) directly addresses hearing voices.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, actually... I did. When I was working at the register, I started hearing voices. It sounded exactly like customers were standing right behind me, just whispering my name. Or they would say things about how I was messing everything up. But every time I turned around to look, nobody was there. It was really strange.

inference.note: The manic episode is confirmed as severe with psychotic features (auditory hallucinations, significant functional impairment, crisis intervention), establishing a Bipolar I history (ruling out F31.2 as the current state since that episode has resolved). The current episode is depressive; F31.4 and F31.5 are now the candidates, differentiated by whether psychotic features are present during this depressive episode - this still needs clarification.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or delusions) are present during the current depressive episode, not just during the earlier manic period, to distinguish severe depression with vs without psychotic features
doctor.question: Now, during this current period of feeling down and exhausted, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having beliefs that others might find unusual or hard to shake?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: The whispering voices only happened during that wired stretch when I was barely sleeping, taking on too much at work, and feeling like my mind was speeding. I never heard them before that, and once my mood crashed into the low period, the voices stopped.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (hearing voices) or delusions are occurring during the current depressive episode (feeling down and exhausted). This relates to the timing of psychotic features, specifically whether they only occurred during the manic episode.

patient.answer: No, not right now. The whispering voices... they really only happened during that wired stretch, you know? When I was barely sleeping, trying to do a million things at work, and my brain just felt like it was racing all the time. I had never heard them before that. And once I crashed and started feeling so exhausted and down, the voices just stopped. So, no, I haven't heard or seen anything unusual lately.

inference.note: Manic episode caused severe functional impairment (removed responsibilities, avoidance, crisis intervention) and included mood-congruent psychotic features (hearing whispering voices), confirming psychotic mania rather than nonpsychotic mania. This rules out F31.4 and narrows diagnosis to F31.5 (Bipolar I disorder, current or most recent episode manic, severe with psychotic features), now in depressive phase.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current major depressive episode of ~4 months duration (persistent depressed mood, anhedonia across multiple domains, unintentional weight loss/appetite disturbance, profound fatigue not relieved by rest) that follows a distinct prior manic episode lasting about one month (decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, excessive involvement in pleasurable/risky activities such as impulsive spending and reorganizing, and functional impairment including workplace errors, being removed from duties, social withdrawal, and need for crisis intervention). During the manic episode, the patient also experienced auditory hallucinations (mood-congruent, occurring only during the high-energy period), confirming psychotic features accompanied the illness course. Endocrine/thyroid symptoms were ruled out. The combination of a clear manic episode with psychotic features followed by a severe depressive episode establishes a Bipolar I Disorder diagnosis, currently in a severe depressive phase with a history of psychotic features, coded as F31.5.
